judge.agent: GPT via src/RimMandrake/Utils/gpt_consult.py (codex.exe), no maker context; the worker that files this did not write the draft

brief:
You are an independent DESIGN JUDGE for a RimWorld 1.6 mod project. You did not write the draft you are judging. Decide on the written constraints only.

ARTIFACT: `nightside_ice_roster_draft_2026-10-05.md` (attached) — a roster draft for the Nightside Ice biome (the mod is now called SleepingIce; same biome).
GOVERNING DESIGN DOC (frozen, owner-ratified): excerpts of `sleeping_ice.md` (attached as biome_sections.md: §4 biology, §4c tunneler slate, §5 always true, §6 never true (hard bans), §7 uniquely available, roster consequences, owed).
OWNER RULINGS ALREADY MADE: `bedazzle_s8.md` (attached: build order rows 2-8, hessarund "only a landform", the passed marks incl. kesshet, the Cold Ledger rite) and `rulings_extra.md` (one biome per animal; RM_ tier for invented names; no biome-specific sun or heat).
Further standing rulings, quoted:
- "Always assume all the dlcs." (no DLC-less path)
- No worldgen of any kind (planet generation). Map generation (GenSteps on a colony map) is ordinary and allowed.
- "If it flies in the fiction, it flies in the game." Flyers get real flight.
- Every mod ships superb Mod Settings: on/off per major feature.
- "no animal or pawn ever vanishes without a readable sign."
- The six ruled organisms (sohl, shivven, frissim, wyrmlet, dhorrumak, hessarund) are admitted already by the owner; the 2026-10-29 triage says "The six ruled organisms stay as they are." Shivven is BUILT.

QUESTION. For each of the ten organisms give a verdict:
- the six ruled ones: KEEP (already admitted) unless the DRAFT DETAIL under the name breaks a §6 ban or a quoted ruling, in which case CHANGE with the exact fix.
- the four new ones (saallen, oolm, neshkoll, ice-kept dead): KEEP, CUT or CHANGE. CUT or CHANGE must quote the violated constraint and its source (section number). Judge: does it fit §4/§5/§6/§7, does it fill a real empty category, is it buildable at the stated cost, does it duplicate something, does it contradict a passed mark (kesshet passed), is its name in the nightside accent and free of the Abyss -ith/-tha/-ia sound.
Then answer the draft's six §3 questions, each with a one-line decision and reason (Q3 and Q5 are art direction: answer from the written constraints; if the written constraints do not decide it, say UNSURE and give the default you would take).
Also flag any FACTUAL problems in the draft (e.g. a mechanic that contradicts the biome doc, a wrong build-cost estimate).

OUTPUT: ONLY a JSON object, no prose around it:
{"organisms": {"sohl": {"verdict": "KEEP|CUT|CHANGE", "reasons": ["..."], "changes": ["..."]}, "shivven": {...}, "frissim": {...}, "wyrmlet": {...}, "dhorrumak": {...}, "hessarund": {...}, "saallen": {...}, "oolm": {...}, "neshkoll": {...}, "ice_kept_dead": {...}},
 "questions": [{"q": 1, "decision": "...", "reason": "..."}, ... six entries],
 "factual_flags": ["..."]}
inputs: design/RimMandrake/biome_rulings.md (one biome per animal; RM_ tier naming; no biome-specific sun/heat)

reasons: Already admitted. Its single sudden commitment and visibly persistent spent body implement the expressly ruled one-move exception; they do not reopen the general surface-movement ban.
The building-to-pawn-to-building conversion leaves a readable result.
Already admitted and BUILT; the later owner instruction says the six ruled organisms stay as they are.
The draft proposes no replacement behaviour or art. Thermal pursuit within ice, travelling tells and open-ice breaches implement §4c.
shivven.note: BUILT (closed item); its larder is bedazzle §8 row 5

reasons: Already admitted. Thaw-released ground activity is an explicit §4/§4c exception to the general surface-fauna restrictions.
Folded wing-cases do not establish fictional flight. Keep both fiction and implementation flightless.
The refreezing/death discrepancy is flagged below; it is not grounds to revoke admission under the specified verdict rule.
Already admitted. Surfacing to feed where inclusion insects stir is expressly required by §4c.6.
No fast surface pursuit, alternative sensing or other new §6 violation is specified. Reused submerged movement must retain its readable tell.
Already admitted. Sustained-heat and disturbed-nest triggers, open-ice breaches and incident-only presence follow §4c.6 and the hull rule.
The invented name remains RM_; genuine canon material belongs in the Utinni layer.

Keep the admitted, behaviourless mineable ridge. The proposed cold-rejection research role introduces a learned-tech offering where bedazzle §8, row 3 says: "Ship, sound and learned tech stay unfilled for this biome by his choice: passed, not gaps to re-pitch."
changes: Remove the proposed new cold-rejection research role. Retain catalyst crust as the ruled mining yield; ordinary integration into existing crafting does not require a new biome-specific technology.
Keep the ridge entirely without behaviour, as required by bedazzle §8, row 2.

reasons: It fills the requested catalytic-sheet category and adds a useful early visual stage to the existing breach loop. A ground seam crust is not, on the supplied evidence, a revival of the passed hull-crust kesshet.

The scraping promise overstates its defensive effect. §4c, hull rule: "The colony's waste heat softening the surrounding ice IS the breach ring; flooring it is real defence." Removing a crust cannot remove the underlying heat-driven breach eligibility.
changes: Make scraping remove the crust and its additional breach-placement weight only. Warm, unfloored open ice must remain eligible for breaches.
Replace "remove that risk" with an explicit statement that scraping reduces this local preference while cooling or flooring provides the established defence.

reasons: Ancient clonal lobes fill the requested boulder-field/colonial-landform form; the name fits the accent.
Its relationship to sohl is biologically unresolved. §4 says: "A new individual is a piece of an old one that reached a new seam." A sohl fragment cannot silently become an unrelated organism.
The insulating-wall reward is not buildable at the stated cost merely by declaring an insulating stuff stat.
changes: Define oolm explicitly as the sessile clonal stage or colony form of the sohl lineage, rather than an independent species produced by sohl fragmentation.
Track colony identity rather than treating every lobe anywhere on the map as automatically one individual.
Drop the material-dependent wall-insulation promise from the small build, or budget and validate the required heat-transfer implementation separately.
Describe mining hardening as a passive physical response; do not introduce vibration sensing or awareness of remote mining.

reasons: It fills the expressly wanted "chemical-frost formations that are ambiguously alive" category. Treat it as a terrain formation with unresolved biology, not an established rapidly reproducing surface animal.
Its directional heat indication differs from the existing hoarfrost scenery and breach warning. It introduces neither sound sensing nor a learned technology.
The name fits the accent and avoids the Abyss endings. No supplied description establishes duplication of a passed mark.
It directly fills §4's "Corpses and the lost — not fauna, the biome's real population" and §7's well-provisioned dead. Its plain English name is appropriate.
Exposure alone does not establish a warm signal. §4 says sensing is "heat and only heat"; §4c describes a dying body as the signal, while dead bodies are stored under perfect preservation.
changes: Make tunnelers respond to an actual heat source used during extraction, a still-living occupant, or explicitly modelled residual warmth. A cold exposed corpse must not automatically emit heat.
Preserve extracted corpses and gear, and connect any theft to a visible drag/submergence sign and the recoverable larder.
Treat the ledger tablet as an optional proposed prop, not a confirmed requirement of the Cold Ledger rite; the supplied ruling establishes only the rite's admission.

questions.decision: Admit saallen, oolm and ice-kept dead with the listed changes; KEEP neshkoll.
questions.reason: Each addresses a written wanted form or population; their useful distinctions survive without reopening passed marks.
Their long vowels, doubled consonants and consonant endings fit the stated accent; none uses -ith, -tha or -ia, and invented names belong in RM_.

questions.decision: UNSURE; default to retaining the shipped shivven art.
questions.reason: The later ruling retains the built organism; §6 constrains recognisable silhouettes, but pink itself is not banned and the supplied material contains no image on which to judge a new visual violation.

questions.decision: Keep frissim fictionally and mechanically flightless; do not add a native-frissim food harvest.
questions.reason: The admitted ground-inclusion role needs no flight, and §7 says "Not food"; §4c.2 separately and explicitly permits the deposited dayside insect-fall as food.

questions.decision: UNSURE; default to one distinct top-down spent-body graphic.
questions.reason: The rules require a permanent, readable spent state but do not prescribe sprite count; one distinct graphic makes that state clear.
Bedazzle §8 guarantees the hessarund yield without making it exclusive; the other catalytic deposits can share it without creating another resource or reopening the passed hull-crust mark.

factual_flags: Frissim refreezing is described inconsistently: §4 makes inclusion insects dormant outside thaw pulses, but the draft kills them when the ice refreezes. Default to renewed dormancy; actual deaths must leave readable remains rather than silently removing pawns.
The insect-fall is specifically a deposited, freeze-dried dayside swarm (§4c.2), not automatically a release of native frissim. Keep those populations and their food permissions distinct.

Oolm's vanilla insulation claim conflates stuff insulation stats with material-dependent wall heat transfer. Declaring StuffProperties does not by itself implement the promised insulating walls; the XML-plus-tiny-comp estimate omits that work.

The proposed oolm comp counts lobes remaining, but the stated behaviour depends on lobes mined from a particular colony. Those are different measurements, especially if lobes are destroyed, spawned or belong to different pan margins.
The sohl description offers non-heat commitments to fresh seams, but its implementation outline specifies only a heat trigger. The fragment-producing commitment needs an actual trigger if retained.
A cold corpse does not become a thermal beacon merely because it is exposed. The draft must identify and implement the actual source of warmth.
The supplied Cold Ledger ruling does not specify a ledger tablet, an item drop or a corpse-loot requirement. Those details remain proposals.
Rot4 provides four cardinal facings; it does not make a plume point exactly toward an arbitrarily positioned source. Use approximate wording or budget continuous rotation.

The displayed build table is not the ratified execution order: it begins with row-7 hessarund work before row-2 thaw/calving and row-4 sohl. Follow bedazzle §8's ordered backlog and explicitly schedule new work without jumping it.

The small cost estimates are conditional: frissim needs its thaw/calving infrastructure, wyrmlets need feeding and readable submergence behaviour, and ice-kept-dead theft needs the larder and recovery system. Those dependencies are not already completed merely because shivven movement is built.
The draft omits the standing requirement for on/off Mod Settings per major feature from its implementation and cost accounting.
Map-local GenSteps are allowed and are not prohibited planet worldgen. Likewise, subzero ice softening is not inherently liquid water; implementing an actual melt pool would violate §6.

The supplied excerpts do not substantiate claims about installed files, completed art, grep results or exact existing-code reuse. They can be accepted as draft premises, but this written-constraint review does not verify them.
art: The four new organisms' artpipe jobs (nightsideice_newlife_*_v1) are in artpipe done/ but their renders no longer exist on disk and were never collected or judged; each build item re-queues its art through the art-evaluation pipeline. Ruled-cast art is untouched by this verdict.
